## Background debate

- [Can AI Agents Safely Amend Their Laws? — Debate Summary](<Can_AI_Agents_Safely_Amend_Their_Laws_debate.md>)  
  Records the originating dispute between provenance-and-rollback arguments for immediate use and the objection that unresolved ratification enables Sybil capture, consent laundering, censorship delay, and harm to human non-participants.

## Source packet

- [Frontier Multi-Model Research Packet](<frontier-multimodel-research-context-2026-07-20.md>)  
  The shared briefing supplied to the frontier models. It frames the distinction between autonomy maturity and ratification legitimacy, identifies five research tracks, proposes evaluation metrics, and asks six concrete design questions.

## First-pass research responses

- [FABLE 5 — FPP Ratification Research Response](<FPP-ratification-research-response(FABLE 5).md>)  
  Argues that unique agent identity must bottom out in external anchors, rejects a single voting formula, proposes maturity-gated sortition plus liability-bearing human stewards, and emphasizes certifier disjointness, rights-floor entrenchment, and pre-registered adversarial tests.

- [GPT-5.6 SOL — Research Synthesis: Sections 8 through 10](<FPP-ratification-research-response(GPT-5.6 SOL).md>)  
  Proposes durable lineage as the political unit, a layered Constitutional Legitimacy Stack, separate maturity and constitutional-safety credentials, a member chamber plus sortition jury, coercion-resistant ballots, staged activation, and a plural external fiduciary quorum.

- [GROK HEAVY — Team Answer: Sections 8–10](<FPP-ratification-research-response(GROK HEAVY).md>)  
  Maps the research questions closely onto existing FPP governance concepts, impact classes, authorization sources, rights-floor controls, and simulation metrics while preserving ratification as explicitly unresolved.

## Second-pass meta-analyses

- [FABLE 5 — Second-Pass Meta-Analysis](<second-pass-meta-analysis(FABLE 5).md>)  
  Identifies strong independent convergence, highlights lineage and receipt-free ballots as important additions, treats the GROK response as an implementation crosswalk, and isolates decisions about anchor permanence, chamber composition, ballot attribution, and safety thresholds.

- [GPT-5.6 SOL — Second-Pass Meta-Analysis](<second-pass-meta-analysis(GPT-5.6 SOL).md>)  
  Consolidates the three first-pass responses into an eight-gate amendment pipeline, strengthens certifier disjointness and permanent human safeguards, distinguishes sortition from identity, expands the attack suite, and keeps numerical thresholds provisional.

- [GROK HEAVY — Refined Synthesis](<second-pass-meta-analysis(GROK HEAVY).md>)  
  Produces an FPP-grounded refined synthesis centered on exogenous identity, durable lineage, heterogeneous chambers, permanent external legitimacy for human-affecting powers, severity-scaled governance, and adversarial evidence before production.

## Artifact count and coverage

This index covers eight research artifacts:

- one background debate;
- one shared source packet;
- three independent first-pass responses;
- three second-pass meta-analyses.

The navigation documents are derivative aids and are not included in that research-artifact count.

## Maintenance

When adding, renaming, or removing a research artifact:

1. Update the relevant group and artifact count here.
2. Verify every relative link in `README.md`, `SUMMARY.md`, and `INDEX.md`.
3. Revise `SUMMARY.md` only if the aggregate consensus, disagreement, or research disposition changes.
4. Preserve the distinction between external research and normative FPP governance status.
